newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the special session of the Transport Council scheduled on Thursday May 29 had been cancelled after the Swiss authorities modified their figures and conditions on road charges to be applied in Switzerland after 1 January 2005.

Spokesman Constantin Verros briefed on the Energy Council to take place on Tuesday. He said discussions would focus on liberalisation of the gas market, renewable energy sources, EU strategy on renewable energy and policy on climate change. He said there would be a first joint ministerial meeting with Central and Eastern European countries counterparts at 1700/1500 GMT.

Spokesman Josep Coll i Carbo said the agreement with Mexico on mutual recognition of liquor brands would be signed on Tuesday. He said there would be a drink at 1600/1400 GMT in the Breydel dining room.
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the EU representatives would not raise the Boeing/McDonnell Douglas merger at Wednesday's EU/U.S. summit in the Netherlands.

Van der Pas said the negotiations on a so-called mutual recognition agreement (MRA) between the EU and the U.S. continued in Paris. He added that the member states' ministers were ready to gather if an agreement was reached.

Spokesman Patrick Child said the German authorities had not formally informed the Commission that they would revalue their gold reserves but that there were constant contacts between Eurostat and the member states on this issue.
Child also said that there were discussions taking place on a common treatment for national central banks reserves.

- IP/97/442: Commission proposes macro-financial assistance for Bulgaria.

- IP/97/444: Extraordianary transport council is cancelled.
